title: Can Large Language Models Capture Video Game Engagement?
abstract: arXiv:2502.04379v3 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Can out-of-the-box pretrained Large Language Models (LLMs) detect human affect successfully when observing a video? To address this question, for the first time, we evaluate comprehensively the capacity of popular LLMs for successfully predicting continuous affect annotations of videos when prompted by a sequence of text and video frames in a multimodal fashion. In this paper, we test LLMs' ability to correctly label changes of in-game engagement in 80 minutes of annotated videogame footage from 20 first-person shooter games of the GameVibe corpus. We run over 4,800 experiments to investigate the impact of LLM architecture, model size, input modality, prompting strategy, and ground truth processing method on engagement prediction. translated_title: 大语言模型能否捕捉视频游戏的玩家参与度？
translated_abstract: 开箱即用的预训练大语言模型（LLM）在观察视频时能否成功检测人类情感？为了回答这个问题，我们首次全面评估了流行的大语言模型在以多模态方式接收文本和视频帧序列提示时，成功预测视频连续情感标注的能力。在本文中，我们使用来自GameVibe语料库的20款第一人称射击游戏的80分钟标注视频片段，测试了大语言模型正确标注游戏内参与度变化的能力。我们进行了超过4,800次实验，以研究大语言模型架构、模型规模、输入模态、提示策略和真实值处理方法对参与度预测的影响。我们的研究结果表明，尽管大语言模型在多个领域确实表现出类人的性能，并能够超越传统的机器学习基线，但它们总体上落后于连续标注方法……
tldr: 本文首次全面评估了大语言模型在多模态（文本+视频帧）提示下预测游戏视频玩家参与度的能力，通过4800多项实验发现，尽管LLM能超越传统机器学习基线，但在连续参与度标注任务上总体表现仍落后于专门方法。
en_tdlr: This paper presents the first comprehensive evaluation of LLMs' ability to predict continuous game engagement from multimodal text-and-video prompts, showing through over 4,800 experiments that while LLMs outperform traditional machine learning baselines, they generally fall behind continuous annotation methods.
